claims.text: H.R. 5060, the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act, was introduced by Rep. Tim Burchett in the 119th Congress; its predecessor was H.R. 10111 in the 118th.
Lawmakers took up the bill in the run-up to the 9 September 2025 UAP transparency hearing specifically because existing channels were judged inadequate for UAP witnesses.

desc: The UAP Whistleblower Protection Act, introduced by Rep. Tim Burchett in the 119th Congress as H.R. 5060, reintroducing H.R. 10111 from the 118th. Its existence is a legislative finding about AARO: Congress would not need to build a separate statutory protection channel for UAP witnesses if the secure reporting mechanism AARO launched at aaro.mil in October 2023 were functioning as a safe destination. The FY2025 annual report's own numbers illustrate the problem - 262 people contacted the mechanism and 255 were declared out of scope. The bill moved onto the agenda in the run-up to the 9 September 2025 House Oversight Task Force hearing, at which Dylan Borland testified to career obstruction and sustained harassment after reporting a UAP at Langley in 2012, and at which Congress heard that witnesses coming forward risk career damage and retaliation.
